comment: amd-rig PHONE HITL bench catalog — read by a SECOND hitl-reserved instance on amd-rig (the phone daemon, //pi/hitl:hitl_sdr's hitl-phone-daemon.nix), separate from the SDR daemon (catalog-sdr.json). Unlike the SDR bench (one privileged, --net-host composite unit), this daemon runs the ISOLATED multi-DUT model (--raw-usb, per-unit sshd ports, bridge networking) so the two phone units run CONCURRENTLY without colliding on adb's fixed port 5037 / the emulator console ports (each reservation gets its own network namespace). Two independent units, each with its OWN C6 (user decision: two C6s/location). host/workspace + the unit sshd port range are passed as flags by hitl-phone-daemon.nix, not baked here.

components.comment: The real-phone unit's C6 DUT. FILL the by-id serial from the live rig: `ls /dev/serial/by-id` on amd-rig (usb-Espressif_USB_JTAG_serial_debug_unit_<MAC>-if00). Pinned to /dev/ttyACM0 in the env so the toolbox (hitl-flash/monitor) works unchanged. Distinct from the SDR bench's C6 and from c6-b below.
components.name: c6-a

components.comment: The emulator unit's C6 DUT (second board). FILL its by-id serial too.
components.name: c6-b

components.comment: The Android dev device (USB). adb enumerates it by its device serial (HITL_ANDROID_SERIAL, from `adb devices`); pass its raw-USB node so the isolated env can reach it. FILL the by-id/by-path from the live rig: adb devices → the serial; `ls -l /dev/serial/by-id` won't list a phone (not a CDC-serial), so use the phone's /dev/bus/usb by-path or a udev-created symlink (see hitl-phone-daemon.nix udev rule). Placeholder maps a stable by-path; adjust to the actual phone.
components.name: android-dev

components.comment: KVM acceleration for the x86_64 Android emulator (amd-rig is x86_64, so the upstream nixpkgs emulator + an x86_64 system image run at native speed under /dev/kvm). Passed as a device into the emulator unit's env; the kvm group + udev give the agent uid access (hitl-phone-daemon.nix).
components.name: kvm

units.comment: REAL-PHONE unit: the Android dev device + its C6. The client reserves it, ships the phone-HITL harness + web bundle into the env, and runs phone_e2e --phone-target android-phone there: it serves the app + driver WS locally, `adb reverse`s them + the forwarded C6 wss to the phone, opens Chrome at ?driver=…&ble=real, and the PHONE provisions the real C6 over its own radio (real Web Bluetooth) → maps/solves end to end. Not pin_only: a bare `--require-caps adb,real-ble` request should match it.
units.name: android-phone

units.comment: EMULATOR unit: a C6 + KVM. The env boots the x86_64 Android emulator (baked in the image, withAndroid) and drives the app in it (10.0.2.2 host alias); BLE is the app-seam virtual mock or the Bumble peripheral (ble_peripheral.py), and the app connects the forwarded real-C6 wss for the map/solve. pin_only so a caps-only request never lands the emulator slot.
units.name: android-emu
